高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)病毒正在哺乳动物中扩大其宿主范围,引发对其大流行潜力的担忧。基于近期发表的深度突变扫描(deep mutational scanning, DMS)数据,研究人员表明,血凝素(hemagglutinin, HA)保留了通过独立机制增强酸稳定性的结构可塑性,这些机制包括调节静电相互作用、氢键网络和疏水堆积,可能促进人类适应性。这些发现阐明了结构分析如何加强基因组监测以进行大流行风险评估。 论文解读文章 Twist Bioscience全面外显子组组合资料免费索取>>领 取 一、研究背景与科学问题 禽流感A(H5N1)病毒,特别是分支2.3.4.4b毒株,正在全球范围内持续传播,引发了其可能引发未来大流行的严重关切。尽管该病毒在人类中的死亡率较以往H5N1疫情有所降低,但其在野生和家养鸟类中的空前传播、感染多种哺乳动物物种的能力以及哺乳动物间传播的证据,均凸显了其人畜共患潜力。2024年,美国奶牛群中出现了持续的哺乳动物间传播,病毒在乳腺中高效复制并在牛奶中产生高病毒载量,表明病毒正在持续适应哺乳动物宿主,这可能促进人类感染。 人类感染禽流感病毒通常效率低下,原因在于多种宿主屏障,如受体识别不佳和与宿主细胞机制不兼容。血凝素(HA)作为主要的三聚体刺突糖蛋白,是宿主特异性的关键决定因素,负责受体结合和膜融合。HA单体被切割为HA1和HA2两个亚基,HA1的球状头部结合宿主受体,HA2形成三聚体中的茎部并将HA三聚体锚定在病毒包膜上。HA2茎区是融合前亚稳态构象的核心决定因素,在流感病毒亚型中高度保守。 融合前中性pH形式的HA三聚体处于亚稳态——足够稳定以在传播过程中存活,又准备好响应内涵体酸化而重折叠。如果HA三聚体过于不稳定,可能过早丧失融合能力;反之,如果过于稳定,融合可能失败。因此,最佳的酸稳定性和pH依赖性激活对病毒感染性至关重要。从禽类病毒(融合触发pH约5.7–6.0)到人类毒株(约5.0–5.5)的适应通常需要进一步稳定化,以增强在空气传播和通过人类呼吸道轻度酸性环境时的存活能力。 H5N1分支2.3.4.4b的出现体现了这一适应性轨迹。该分支约于2020年通过高致病性禽H5N8毒株与低致病性禽病毒之间的重组产生,此后在全球传播。尽管该分支的HA仍主要结合禽型α2,3-连接唾液酸受体,对人类型α2,6-连接受体亲和力较弱,但实验研究表明,少数HA突变即可改变受体特异性并增强酸稳定性,使雪貂等哺乳动物能够通过空气传播。然而,这些突变在流行毒株中仍然罕见,表明高效的人类适应需要多个协调变化。此外,HA胞外域(ectodomain, ECD)在低pH下的稳定化对于呼吸道飞沫酸性条件下的空气传播能力至关重要。 本研究旨在检验H5N1分支2.3.4.4b血凝素胞外域的酸稳定性和结构适应,重点关注可能增强低pH稳定性从而促进人类宿主适应的突变。研究人员基于Dadonaite等人(2024)对循环H5N1病毒ECD稳定性的综合分析,探索增强酸稳定性的分子决定因素及其对哺乳动物适应的潜在贡献,为理解增强的酸稳定性如何影响H5N1分支2.3.4.4b的进化轨迹和人畜共患潜力提供机制框架。 二、主要技术方法 研究人员以H5 A/Texas/37/2024(pdb 9DIP)的三维晶体结构为参考,该毒株是分支2.3.4.4b的参考株,与Dadonaite等人(2024)分析的A/American Wigeon/South Carolina/2021毒株具有99.4%的序列一致性,序列差异仅限三个位点(Leu122Gln、Thr200Ile和Asp240Asn)。研究人员使用PyMOL(版本3.0.2)分析HA结构,预测突变对极性相互作用和表面电势的影响;使用自适应泊松-玻尔兹曼求解器(Adaptive Poisson-Boltzmann Solver, APBS)结合PDB2PQR软件(AMBER力场),在0.15 M NaCl条件下计算pH 5.3和7.4的表面电势,以表征突变在酸性和中性范围内对电势的影响。 三、研究结果 稳定化突变在HA1亚基中的分布与机制 HA1亚基中可稳定ECD的突变残基主要位于头部结构域下部、茎区上方以及ECD茎部的小区域。 Glu31Lys:Glu31位于ECD表面。该稳定化突变导致与Arg321的极性相互作用丧失,但仍保留与Thr28的相互作用。由于该位点处于负电荷环境中,正电荷残基(如赖氨酸)可在酸性pH下稳定融合前构象。 Lys57Glu和Lys62Glu:这两个突变局部降低了该区域主导的正表面电势。在酸性pH下,正表面电势的降低减少了其排斥性质,从而有助于ECD的稳定化。 Arg81Gly:该突变通过改变表面电势稳定融合前构象。Arg81位于具有正电势的HA1头部结构域,突变为甘氨酸降低了该区域的排斥性质,尤其在酸性pH下。此外,Arg81邻近高度疏水的残基Ile80和Phe79,疏水环境对ECD稳定性至关重要。 Arg90Glu:该突变降低局部正表面电势,从而可能有助于ECD在酸性pH下的稳定性。 Glu106Asp:该突变极大增强了稳定性。天冬氨酸的引入保留了与Asn71(2)的现有相互作用,同时与相邻单体的Arg76(2)形成额外相互作用。因此,该突变不仅稳定了单体内部的HA1-HA2界面,还稳定了两个单体之间的HA1-HA2界面。 Lys109:该位点位于HA1头部结构域的短螺旋中。Lys109Ala和Lys109Gln两个突变在酸性pH下稳定融合前构象。Lys109Gln突变比Lys109Ala更具稳定性,可能归因于与Tyr105的极性相互作用。 Lys262Ile:该突变体在pH 5.3下仍保持稳定。Lys262邻近其他正电荷残基(Arg81、Lys109和Lys269),这些残基在酸性pH下因质子化而增强正表面电势的排斥性质。异亮氨酸取代减少了这种效应,从而解释了酸性pH下增强的稳定性。 Lys269Glu:尽管该突变导致与Glu89、Arg90和Ala91的极性相互作用丧失,但局部表面电势的改变可能引起稳定性增加。负电荷的谷氨酸抵消了Lys269质子化引起的局部排斥力。 Val315-Asn104(2):Val315与Asn104(2)之间存在弱极性接触,位于单体的茎区。Val315突变为Arg可形成与Gln25的额外极性键,可能解释其稳定化效应。 Thr318:位于HA茎部靠近融合肽口袋的位置,与His38和His111(2)形成极性相互作用。Thr318Ile突变具有中等稳定化效应,可能归因于异亮氨酸相比苏氨酸更高的疏水性,促进了与相邻HA2亚基残基的相互作用,并可能增强疏水融合肽的嵌入。 稳定化突变在HA2亚基中的分布与机制 HA2茎部和融合肽区域高度保守,对HA三聚体稳定性至关重要,大多数突变具有去稳定化效应。然而,在长螺旋及其与短螺旋的连接区域鉴定出了潜在的稳定化突变。 Asp57(2)Tyr:该突变保留了Asp57(2)与Asn54(2)之间的极性相互作用,同时中和了Asp57(2)在pH 7.4和5.3下的轻微负表面电势。中性氨基酸增强ECD稳定性,而疏水氨基酸则不然。 Arg68(2)Ser:Arg68(2)与Gly67(2)和Glu85(2)形成极性相互作用。邻近的Arg75(2)、Arg76(2)、Lys82(2)和Lys83(2)聚集在Arg68(2)周围,形成局部正表面电势,尤其在酸性pH下。Arg68(2)Ser突变破坏了与Gly67(2)和Glu85(2)的相互作用,但降低了局部正表面电势,这可能解释其稳定化效应。 Ile77(2)Leu:该位点位于HA2亚基的长螺旋中,三个HA2亚基的长螺旋在此紧密靠近。与异亮氨酸不同,三个HA螺旋的亮氨酸之间形成多个疏水相互作用,解释了稳定化效应。 Glu78(2)Phe:野生型中Glu78(2)与Arg75(2)形成盐桥(3.4 ?),并与Glu74(2)、Arg75(2)和Lys82(2)存在极性相互作用。苯丙氨酸突变后仅保留与Glu74(2)和Lys82(2)的极性相互作用。苯丙氨酸引入的高度疏水非极性性质表明,长HA2螺旋顶部的疏水区域可以稳定ECD。 Leu89(2)Glu:Leu89(2)与Glu85(2)和Thr93(2)存在极性相互作用。谷氨酸(和天冬氨酸)突变加强了与Thr93(2)的相互作用,这可能解释其对HA2茎区的稳定化效应。 Asp90(2)Glu:Asp90(2)位于长HA2螺旋中,与螺旋内的残基、相邻HA2螺旋的Gln62(2)以及相邻HA1亚基的Lys307形成极性相互作用网络,包括3.5 ?的盐桥。Asp90(2)Glu突变保留了这一网络,并通过更短的盐桥(2.9 ?)和额外的极性接触加强了与Lys307的相互作用。Asp90(2)Met突变也具有稳定化效应,甲硫氨酸的疏水性质支持核心堆积和结构稳定性。 Val91(2)Met:Val91(2)与Gly87(2)和Asn95(2)之间的极性相互作用被保留。甲硫氨酸侧链朝向三个长HA2螺旋的中心,导致三个甲硫氨酸残基之间的疏水相互作用。 Asp95(2)Glu:相邻长HA2螺旋的Asn95(2)残基之间的极性相互作用被保留。Glu-Glu相互作用(2.5 ?)比Asp-Asp相互作用(2.8 ?)更强。Asp95(2)Met也具有稳定化效应,甲硫氨酸侧链通过疏水作用力(3.0 ?)相互作用。 Leu98(2)Met:该突变保留了与Tyr94(2)和Met102(2)的极性相互作用,并引入与Tyr94(2)、Met102(2)以及相邻HA2螺旋的Ile55(2)的额外疏水相互作用。 Leu99(2)Met:该突变保留了与Asn95(2)和Glu103(2)的极性相互作用,但甲硫氨酸朝向三个长HA2螺旋的中心,形成疏水相互作用网络。 Arg106(2)Glu和Arg106(2)Lys:Arg106(2)与螺旋内的残基及相邻HA2亚基的Glu105(2)形成极性相互作用。Arg106(2)Glu突变中,与Glu105(2)的相互作用丧失,但与同一亚基短HA2螺旋的Lys51(2)形成新的相互作用,由2.6 ?盐桥稳定。稳定化效应也可能源于减少了Arg106(2)侧链在酸性pH下伸入茎中心的排斥作用。 Asn117(2)Glu:Asn117(2)与Ser113(2)和Lys121(2)形成亚基内相互作用,并与相邻HA2亚基的Leu2(2)形成单体间接触,Leu2(2)标记融合肽的N端。Asn117(2)Glu突变导致与Leu2(2)的相互作用丧失,并引起局部表面电势从轻微正值向负值的显著转变,可能通过减少低pH下质子化引起的排斥性质来稳定融合前构象。 组氨酸残基作为HA构象变化的pH传感器 多项研究已确定特定组氨酸残基是触发HA构象变化的关键pH传感器。组氨酸的质子化状态在生理pH范围(pH 7–6)内发生变化,使其独特地适合这一角色。在A/Texas/37/2024的HA单体ECD中共有16个组氨酸残基,其中四个位于HA2亚基。除His111(2)外,所有残基均位于ECD表面。已被提出作为pH依赖性构象变化可能触发因子的保守组氨酸残基包括HA1中的His18和His184,以及HA2中的His111(2)和His142(2)。 四、结论与意义 HA1中稳定化突变主要位于头部结构域下部,通过降低局部正表面电荷或加强分子间和分子内相互作用发挥作用。Glu31Lys、Lys57Glu和Arg90Glu等取代降低了酸性条件下的静电排斥,而Glu106Asp和Thr318Ile等突变通过额外的极性接触或融合肽附近的疏水堆积增强稳定性。HA2中潜在稳定化突变主要发生在长螺旋和连接环中,通常通过疏水取代改善螺旋间堆积、加强极性网络或减少带电区域的静电排斥来增加稳定性。甲硫氨酸取代尤其值得注意,因为它们支持螺旋束内的疏水核心堆积。 该研究表明,血凝素保留了通过独立机制增加酸稳定性的结构可塑性,包括调节静电相互作用、氢键网络和疏水堆积。这些发现阐明了结构分析如何加强基因组监测以进行大流行风险评估,为理解增强的酸稳定性如何影响H5N1分支2.3.4.4b的进化轨迹和人畜共患潜力提供了机制框架。高效的人间传播可能需要聚合酶活性、受体结合特异性和HA稳定性三个关键病毒特性的同步适应突变,而本研究对HA稳定性分子决定因素的深入解析为监测和风险评估提供了重要的结构基础。 supplementary_news.content: Skip to main content Skip to news navigation, settings and search Explore the ABC More from ABC news iview listen Log InLog In ABC News Just In For You Politics World Business Analysis More Search Search the ABC Start typing for suggestions, press enter to search, or choose from a list of options below. Cancel News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts ABC News News Home 'Emergency extractions' of wild birds considered as H5 bird flu spreads in Victoria ShareShare article 'Emergency extractions' of wild birds considered as H5 bird flu spreads in Victoria By Annie Brown ABC Rural Topic:Avian Influenza Posted Sat at 8:17pmSaturday at 8:17pmSat 26 Sep 2026 at 8:17pm There are about 1,000 brolgas left in the wild in Victoria. (ABC Rural: Annie Brown) In short: The Victorian government is considering "emergency extractions" of threatened bird species from the wild, as H5 avian influenza spreads. The breeding season has commenced in Victorian wetlands this spring, increasing the risk of bird flu circulating among the congregating fauna. What's next? The government has identified nearly 100 bird species at risk of H5N1, including black swans and brolgas. Northern Victoria is home to thousands of individual wetlands on public and private property, and in September they are brimming with birdlife. With spring comes the breeding season, when many threatened species like brolgas and black swans congregate, make nests, lay eggs and hatch fledglings. Black swans are considered to be at high risk of H5 bird flu. (ABC Rural: Annie Brown) This year, there is another threat, the H5N1 strain of avian influenza, which is spreading through the wild bird population. That risk has led the Victorian government to consider "emergency extractions" of threatened bird species from the wild for protection. Chief biodiversity officer at the Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action (DEECA), James Todd said he was concerned the already small populations could plummet. James Todd is concerned about vulnerable fauna in Victoria. (Supplied: Arthur Rylah Institute) "We are looking at whether there's also some direct interventions that we can undertake for ... species that are not yet in captivity," Mr Todd said. "We might consider doing some sort of emergency extraction." Zoos Victoria and other wildlife facilities already have populations of threatened species in captivity to ensure their protection. "That's the orange-bellied parrot, plains wanderer, regent honeyeater, and the helmeted honeyeater, one of the state's formal emblems," Mr Todd said. Although it is uncertain what will happen with the spread of H5N1, Mr Todd said there were no reported cases worldwide of a species going extinct yet. "That's kind of the light on the hill," he said. "But again, we have to be careful because we can't exactly translate the overseas experience to Australia and Victoria because of our unique fauna." The regent honey eater has a population of fewer than 250 in the wild. (Supplied: Jo Howell/Zoos Victoria) Victorian Brolgas already under threat Victoria's population of brolgas sits around 1,000, with most found in the south-west of the state. In northern Victoria and southern New South Wales, that number is even smaller, with an estimated population of 50, making them an incredibly rare sight. Brolgas are common in northern Australia but are listed as endangered in Victoria. (ABC Rural: Annie Brown) Mr Todd said the Victorian population was effectively isolated from the central Australian brolga population "where they're obviously much more abundant and common and not threatened." The low numbers have been attributed to habitat loss and predation from introduced species like foxes. "They've been impacted by loss of habitat, you know, because of agriculture and urbanisation areas and they rely on temporary wetlands," Mr Todd said. Ducks and waterfowl are breeding in Victorian wetlands during spring. (ABC Rural: Annie Brown) Farmers protecting wetlands Just outside Rushworth, among the fields of wheat and canola, Adrian Weston has about 8 hectares of wetland on his farm. Adrian Weston (left) with Rushworth Field and Game volunteers on the farm's wetland. (ABC Rural: Annie Brown) Mr Weston purchased the property 35 years ago, and was the former director of the Goulburn Broken Catchment Management Authority. He said he had seen a shift over the past 30 years, with more farmers helping to conserve them. "I think out of the 3,000-odd wetlands in the Goulburn Broken catchment, the overwhelming majority of them are on private land and a lot of them got drained," Mr Weston said. "Over time I've seen a shift in the attitudes toward incorporating ... more ecological outcomes into farm enterprise." Mr Weston said he hoped to leave the land better than when he found it, but he had also found lots of productive benefits as well. Black swans nest in wetlands around Rushworth. (ABC Rural: Annie Brown) This year, Mr Weston has witnessed brolgas nesting in the wetland, and has seen a chick hatch. Each week, the Rushworth Field and Game group of volunteers and some of the students from the local school come to Mr Weston's wetland and check hen houses and nest boxes for any activity. During the year, the Field and Game group also hunt foxes to keep numbers low around the wetlands. Black swans are at risk from the H5N1 strain of avian influenza. (ABC Rural: Annie Brown) Mr Weston said he was concerned about the impact H5 avian influenza will have on the wetland birds. "There's a lot at stake," Mr Weston said. "I suppose we hope for the best, but time will tell." Close menuABC ABC News ABC iview ABC listen Kids & Students Indigenous Information & Services

supplementary_news.content: Health & Oddar Meanchey Man Tests Positive for Bird Flu After Handling Infected Chickens A 49-year-old man in Oddar Meanchey is receiving hospital treatment after testing positive for H5N1 due to having direct contact with sick and dead chickens that also tested positive for the virus Chickens being fed in their coops in Battambang province. Kiripost/Meas Molika Chhorn Raksmey & Published on: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 - 10:47 AM(GMT+7) ~ 2 min read 0 Share To: x1 00:00 / 02:03 A 49-year-old man in Oddar Meanchey province has tested positive for H5N1 bird flu after coming into direct contact with sick and dead chickens, according to the Ministry of Health (MoH). The man, from Toul Kruos village in O Svay commune, Trapeang Prasat district, tested positive for H5N1 at the National Institute of Public Health and Institut Pasteur du Cambodge, the MoH said in a statement on September 27. “The patient is currently isolated in a hospital and is receiving intensive medical care,” the MoH stated. The patient was a chicken breeder and caretaker on a farm and had direct contact with sick and dead chickens that were also found to have tested positive for H5N1 avian influenza by the National Institute of Animal Health and Animal Production on September 23, 2026. An emergency response team​, working with Ministry of Agriculture Forestry and Fisheries​ officials, has​​ investigated the case to identify people who may have been in contact with the infected birds. The team​ also provided Tamiflu to people who directly touched the dead birds, and have also launched a campaign to raise awareness of the illness in the patient’s village. Ly Sovann, Director of the Communicable Disease Control Department (CDC) and MoH spokesperson, said between 2024 and November 2025, H5N1 bird flu caused 15 deaths among 34 cases recorded in Cambodia. The CDC previously stated that the best way to prevent H5N1 is to avoid touching sick or dead birds, poultry or any materials, such as bedding or litter, contaminated by their bodily fluids, and to observe all animals from a safe distance. It also advised people to cook eggs, poultry and beef properly to kill viruses and to avoid consuming raw milk or raw milk products, particularly those sourced from animals suspected of having avian influenza. supplementary_news.content: 新型H5N1流感血凝素变异体唾液酸结合能力减弱的人类感染病例研究 《Nature Communications》:Diminished sialoside binding in novel H5N1 influenza hemagglutinin variants identified in a human patient 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年09月29日 来源:Nature Communications 18.1 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Article Open access 2024年,加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省一名青少年女性因感染新型H5N1流感毒株(BC24)住院,出现包括呼吸衰竭在内的严重症状。研究人员使用冷冻电子显微镜(cryo-EM)技术发现,在既往研究的H5血凝素(HA)蛋白唾液酸结合位点中发现的N169 α2,3-连接自身聚糖,在纯化的BC24 HA蛋白中缺失,这表明其对α2,3-连接唾液酸苷的亲和力显著降低。糖芯片(glycan microarray)和酶联免疫吸附测定(ELISA)分析显示,BC24病例中鉴定出的HA变异体对α2,3-连接唾液酸苷和α2,6-连接唾液酸苷均表现出严重降低或完全缺失的结合能力。在A549肺泡癌细胞中表达的全长BC24 HA能够驱动膜融合,尽管融合水平低于既往的H5 HA蛋白;患者感染后血清与BC24 HA及其他流感亚型HA蛋白均表现出强结合能力。由于两个目标突变各自独立及联合作用时均能严重降低唾液酸苷结合能力,该病例中似乎存在多个受体结合表型减弱的病毒群体。BC24病例中弱结合HA变异体占据相当比例的少数群体,揭示了严重禽流感感染中可能存在的因素具有更多复杂性。 **研究背景与科学问题** 欢迎下载《抗体人源化服务全流程解析》》 领 取 H5N1禽流感病毒在牛和鸟类中的暴发引起了对人畜共患传播的高度关注,确诊病例的病死率接近50%。2024年11月,加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省一名青少年女性因感染新型H5N1流感毒株(A/British Columbia/PHL-2032/2024,简称BC24)住院,出现包括呼吸衰竭在内的严重症状。该毒株属于分支2.3.4.4b,由于未能从患者体内分离出完整病毒,研究人员通过对症状出现后第八天气管抽吸物(下呼吸道样本)进行测序,揭示了患者体内存在混合病毒群体。除聚合酶碱性蛋白2中已知的E627K突变外,该患者H5N1序列中观察到的最常见突变是血凝素(hemagglutinin,HA)蛋白中的E190D和Q226H(以H3序列编号),各约占测序读数的三分之一。 HA是流感A病毒感染所必需的表面糖蛋白,负责结合宿主细胞受体并介导病毒与宿主内体膜的融合。HA的宿主受体通常为唾液酸苷:含α2,3-连接唾液酸(N-乙酰神经氨酸,N-acetylneuraminic acid,Neu5Ac)的受体常被视为禽类受体,含α2,6连接者常被视为人类受体。既往研究表明,E190D突变在H1 HA中与G225D协同可介导受体特异性向α2,6-连接唾液酸苷转换,但单独的E190D突变并未表现出促进唾液酸亲和力;HA第226位亮氨酸可赋予α2,6-连接唾液酸苷结合能力,但组氨酸在该位置未观察到类似效应。BC24病例中同时出现的E190D和Q226H突变是否导致HA受体特异性改变尚不清楚。为探究这些突变对HA结构和功能的影响,研究人员对BC24 HA以及两个参考毒株——分支1的A/Vietnam/1203/2004(VN04)和引起轻度人类疾病的分支2.3.4.4b A/Michigan/90/2024(MI24)——进行了系统研究。 **研究内容与主要结论** 该研究通过冷冻电子显微镜(cryogenic electron microscopy,cryo-EM)解析了三种H5 HA蛋白三聚体胞外域的前融合态结构,发现BC24 microarray)技术系统评估HA蛋白对N-连接和O-连接聚糖的結合谱;利用酶联免疫吸附测定(ELISA)定量检测HA突变体对代表性α2,3-和α2,6-连接唾液酸苷的结合能力;利用基于NanoBiT荧光素酶重组系统的细胞-细胞膜融合实验评估HA介导膜融合的功能;利用动态光散射(dynamic light scattering,DLS)验证蛋白制品的均一性和稳定性;利用生物层干涉测量技术(biolayer interferometry,BLI)评估广谱中和抗体MEDI8852 Fab与HA的结合动力学。样本来源于加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省儿童医院确诊的BC24患者及年龄匹配的健康对照者血清。 **研究结果** **1. BC24 HA中N169 α2,3-连接自身聚糖密度缺失** 通过cryo-EM结构解析,VN04和MI24 HA蛋白的受体结合位点中均清晰观察到此前报道的N169自身聚糖密度,该聚糖被建模为GlcNAc-GlcNAc-Man-Man-GlcNAc-Gal-Sia,末端糖苷键为α2,3构型。然而,携带E190D和Q226H突变的BC24 HA的受体结合位点中未观察到该自身聚糖密度。由于三种HA蛋白的受体结合位点残基构象高度相似(RMSD值均小于0.45 ?),且BC24和MI24使用相同表达系统、序列相似性高,排除糖基化缺失的可能性,该结果表明BC24 HA对α2,3-连接唾液酸苷的亲和力降低是突变导致的特异性相互作用丧失所致。 **2. BC24与其他H5 HA蛋白糖基化模式比较** 在N21、N33、N158(仅VN04)、N169、N289和N483位点均观察到N-连接糖基化密度。N169位点仅在VN04和MI24 HA中解析出超出初始部分的密度,与这些聚糖结合在受体结合位点一致。N21和N158位点可见连接糖基的密度,但糖基本身可能无序而无法可靠建模。N158位糖基化此前被报道可中等程度遮蔽受体结合位点影响嗜性,而分支2.3.4.4b HA序列缺乏该糖基化位点,可能有助于人类感染性。 **3. E190D和Q226H突变体ELISA糖结合评估** 在MI24背景下引入E190D和Q226H突变(正向突变)以及在BC24背景下引入D190E和H226Q回复突变,构建了所有可能的单突变和双突变组合。ELISA结果显示,携带D190或H226的任何突变体均对α2,3-和α2,6-连接唾液酸苷无可检测的结合,而回复突变D190E+H226Q恢复了BC24 HA对α2,3-连接唾液酸苷的结合能力。该结果表明E190D和Q226H各自均可独立导致唾液酸苷结合能力严重降低。 **6. HA缺乏与N169自身聚糖的结合;糖芯片和ELISA证实其既不结合α2,3-也不结合α2,6-连接唾液酸苷;突变实验表明E190D和Q226H各自独立即可导致该表型。值得注意的是,BC24 研究人员提出,弱受体结合表型可能有利于病毒逃避上呼吸道受体而富集于下呼吸道远端,与BC24病例中下呼吸道病毒载量较高和病程较重的临床表现相符。然而,该病例未发生人传人传播,与α2,6-连接唾液酸苷结合促进人际传播的普遍认知一致。患者血清中检测到对H5 HA的强烈抗体反应和广泛的亚型交叉反应性,且HA仍可被广谱中和抗体MEDI8852有效中和,病毒对常规抗流感药物保持敏感,这些发现缓解了近期公共卫生紧急事件的担忧,但也提示严重禽流感感染中病毒适应机制可能比以往认识的更为复杂。受体结合强度并非人感染致病性的唯一决定因素这一观察,对流感大流行风险评估和人畜共患监测策略具有重要意义。 BC24患者体液免疫反应**对BC24患者四个时间点(血清Flu A RT-PCR转阴后1-4天)及四名年龄匹配健康对照者的血清进行ELISA检测。健康对照者对BC24和MI24 HA表现出中等反应性,推测为疫苗接种或季节性流感感染产生的交叉反应抗体。BC24患者血清对BC24和MI24 HA均表现出强反应性,且对H1、H2和H3 HA蛋白均表现出明显高于健康对照的交叉反应性,包括对非循环的H2N2毒株HA的高稀释度阳性信号,说明患者对感染产生了强效体液免疫应答,但仍未能防止严重疾病的发生。**讨论与结论**该研究的结构、生化和细胞实验一致证明BC24 HA对α2,3-连接唾液酸苷的亲和力严重降低。cryo-EM结构显示BC24 HA缺乏与N169自身聚糖的结合;糖芯片和ELISA证实其既不结合α2,3-也不结合α2,6-连接唾液酸苷;突变实验表明E190D和Q226H各自独立即可导致该表型。值得注意的是,BC24 HA仍保留膜融合能力且融合水平高于Y98F严重降低受体结合突变体,提示弱结合变异体在患者体内仍具有功能适应性。该案例不支持此前提出的E190D和Q226H突变可能使HA受体特异性从α2,3-向α2,6-连接唾液酸苷转换的假说。研究人员提出,弱受体结合表型可能有利于病毒逃避上呼吸道受体而富集于下呼吸道远端,与BC24病例中下呼吸道病毒载量较高和病程较重的临床表现相符。然而,该病例未发生人传人传播,与α2,6-连接唾液酸苷结合促进人际传播的普遍认知一致。患者血清中检测到对H5 HA的强烈抗体反应和广泛的亚型交叉反应性,且HA仍可被广谱中和抗体MEDI8852有效中和,病毒对常规抗流感药物保持敏感,这些发现缓解了近期公共卫生紧急事件的担忧,但也提示严重禽流感感染中病毒适应机制可能比以往认识的更为复杂。受体结合强度并非人感染致病性的唯一决定因素这一观察,对流感大流行风险评估和人畜共患监测策略具有重要意义。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! 公测期:打赏8元解锁30天免费阅读!

has achieved landmark victories across multiple industries — from pharmaceuticals and agriculture to entertainment and commercial trafficking of animals. Modernizing the $1.35 Trillion Pharmaceutical Industry and Reducing Animal Testing Through our Modernize Testing campaign, the Center led efforts to end the federal mandate for animal testing in drug development. MORE ABOUT OUR CAMPAIGN Ending the Use of Kangaroo Leather in Major Sportswear Companies Our Kangaroos Are Not Shoes campaign convinced the top nine global athletic shoe brands, including Nike, Puma, Adidas, and New Balance, to abandon kangaroo leather in soccer cleats. MORE ABOUT OUR CAMPAIGN Promoting and Defending Cage-Free Animal Agriculture Our Cage-Free Future campaign helped uphold California's Prop 12 and other state laws limiting in-state sales of animal products from factory farms using immobilizing crates and cages. MORE ABOUT OUR CAMPAIGN Crippling the Global Cockfighting Crime Syndicate Through our Animal Fighting Is the Pits campaign, the Center helped outlaw cockfighting in all U.S. jurisdictions — including the U.S. territories. MORE ABOUT OUR CAMPAIGN Breaking the Dairy Monopoly in Public Schools Our Dunking the Milk Mandate campaign led the congressional campaign to end the 80-year-old cow’s milk mandate in the National School Lunch Program, bringing choice in the form of plant-based milks to kids in schools. MORE ABOUT OUR CAMPAIGN Eliminating Greyhound Racing In our Ban Greyhound Racing campaign, the Center supported the Florida ballot initiative to ban greyhound racing, closing 12 tracks and collapsing two-thirds of the U.S. industry overnight. MORE ABOUT OUR CAMPAIGN HOW we do it 1. Evaluating Issues Priority issues are determined based on the numbers of animals affected and level of animal suffering. 2. Conducting Campaigns We research techniques and partnerships to lead campaigns on a number of corporate animal welfare issues. 3. Engaging Corporations Companies are evaluated on their policies and practices regarding the specific animal welfare issue, and we use our campaigns to convince them to transition from harmful to humane animal practices. 4. Educating Consumers We target our campaigns to multiple media outlets, alerting consumers to corporate animal welfare issue transgressors as well as innovators and companies leading their field in alternatives to animal use. We need not accept the idea of routine cruelty in agriculture, entertainment, wildlife management, or any other part of our economy and culture. Together, by reinforcing what business leaders are doing and ready to do, we can create a new normal when it comes to our human relationship with animals. — Wayne Pacelle, The Humane Economy: How Innovators and Enlightened Consumers Are Transforming the Lives of Animals ACT NOW to give voice to the voiceless You can easily send an email that will benefit animals by clicking ACT NOW below. They advised visitors to the park not to approach, feed or come into close contact with the birds. According to initial information, a woman noticed the goose behaving abnormally in recent days. It died the day after she spotted it. The Veterinary Services are continuing laboratory tests with the EU reference laboratory to establish how virulent the virus is, and have informed the European Commission and the World Organisation for Animal Health. Bird flu is a contagious viral disease of birds caused by the influenza A virus. Healthy birds become infected either directly, through contact with infected or sick birds, or indirectly, through contaminated objects. The Veterinary Services said poultry farmers must take all necessary measures to prevent wild or migratory birds from coming into contact with their flocks. Backyard poultry owners must confine their birds to enclosed, covered areas to avoid any direct or indirect contact with wild birds, particularly in communities near wetlands. Keeping poultry outdoors and giving them food and water outside are strictly banned. Owners should also avoid feeding their birds in a way that allows wild birds to eat the food, and must not give poultry water from surface water tanks that wild birds can reach. Under the Animal Health Laws, owners who notice increased illness or deaths among their poultry that raise suspicion of the disease must report it immediately to their district veterinary officer. UNSW on Instagram Follow UNSW on Facebook Follow UNSW on WeChat Follow UNSW on TikTok WhatsApp 2026 annual waterbird survey will also track H5N1 27 September 2026 Photo: Richard Kingsford, UNSW Sydney UNSW Media / Centre for Ecosystem Science, UNSW researchers will survey thousands of wetlands and rivers across eastern Australia this spring, collecting one of the world’s longest-running datasets on waterbird populations – while also looking for signs of H5N1 avian influenza. A team of Australian researchers – led by UNSW’s Centre for Ecosystem Science with the NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water , opens in a new window(DCCEEW) and other state agencies – will begin Australia’s 44th annual waterbird survey tomorrow. The team will cover up to 2000 wetlands and rivers across eastern Australia while monitoring for signs of the highly pathogenic avian influenza, H5N1. During late September to early November, two observers will estimate the waterbird diversity and numbers across a third of the continent from a light plane around 50 metres above water. They will fly for 38,000km – a distance almost equivalent to a round-the-world trip. “We count the numbers of waterbirds on about 2000 wetlands and rivers across eastern Australia, identifying more than 50 species,” says Scientia Professor Richard Kingsford, Director of the Centre for Ecosystem Science, who leads the survey program. In addition to their usual long-term data collection, the team will this year also focus on concentrations of birds that might be affected by H5N1 avian influenza, making it one of the more extensive surveillance programs in Australia – and an important early-warning system as the virus spreads through Australian wildlife. “We were looking out for it last year,” Prof. Kingsford says. “But it has now arrived on the continent. “We will record any mass mortalities we see during aerial surveys – although we will not be able to conclude whether they are natural or due to avian influenza.” Instead, he says the team will report any incidents through the approved protocols and alert relevant state jurisdictions for follow-up. Media enquiries For media enquiries and to arrange interviews, please contact Melissa Lyne: Tel: 0415 514 328 Email: m.lyne@unsw.edu.au Featured expert Richard Kingsford, Lake Eucumbene, aerial waterbird survey, 2025. Photo: Richard Kingsford, UNSW Sydney Beyond the count The annual surveys’ spatial and temporal vastness means it is not only one of the largest wildlife surveys in the world, but also crucial in demonstrating long-term trends in waterbird biodiversity, wetland area and health. This in turn has underpinned major management decisions, says Prof. Kingsford. This year the team are also expecting to see the effects of El-Niño with below-average flooding and drying wetlands associated with current climate conditions across eastern Australia. While extensive wetland areas in the Lake Eyre Basin – including Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre – remain, many individual wetlands are likely drying back. “El-Niño effects are unlikely to be obvious this year, except for the lack of flooding,” Prof. Kingsford says. “But we will probably just start to see big concentrations of waterbirds as they congregate on the shrinking wetland habitat.” He says the survey provides another year of data that will not only bolster the trend analysis but, “continue to inform policy and future environmental management decision making, while also being a tool to monitor the long-term effects of avian influenza outbreaks”. If you’d like to witness these spectacular wetlands, Prof. Kingsford and the team will update a daily blog that includes an interactive map with images and videos of their journey. We will record any mass mortalities we see during aerial surveys. Professor Richard Kingsford The annual survey is run by UNSW’s Centre for Ecosystem Science, supported by resourcing and funding from DCCEEW, with additional funding provided by the South Australian Department for Environment and Water, opens in a new window, the Queensland Government, opens in a new window, the Victorian Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action, opens in a new window, and the Victorian Game Management Authority, opens in a new window. Episodes BannerHealth.com Better Me Teach Me Advise Me Inspire Me By Stephanie Thurrott , Contributing Writer September 28, 2026 Teach Me What Backyard Flock Owners Should Know About Bird Flu If you keep chickens, ducks, geese or turkeys, protecting your backyard flock from bird flu (avian influenza) is important. This flu virus can spread easily and your flock could get infected by contact with wild birds. It’s possible for bird flu to spread to people. This isn’t common but your risk is higher if you’re exposed to infected birds or contaminated surfaces. Corey Casper, MD, an infectious disease specialist with Banner - University Medicine, shared more about how bird flu can spread and symptoms to watch for in birds and people. How backyard birds can be exposed Bird flu, also called avian flu, is widespread in wild birds, even those that don’t look very sick. Your flock could catch it from wild birds near the coop, feeders, water sources or droppings from wild birds. It can spread through: Contaminated shoes, clothing, hands or equipment New birds added to the flock Shared equipment from other flock owners Contact with sick or dead birds Backyard ducks and wild waterfowl may carry the virus without looking sick, making bird flu in ducks harder to spot right away. Signs of bird flu in chickens, ducks and other birds Contact a veterinarian, local agriculture department, extension office or health department if your birds are sick or dying unexpectedly. Watch for signs like: Sudden death Low energy Not eating or drinking Trouble breathing Coughing or sneezing Swelling around the head, neck or eyes Discharge from the eyes or nose Purple discoloration of the comb, wattles or legs Diarrhea Lack of coordination Birds that seem quiet, weak or very sick “Changes in eggs can also matter. Discolored, irregular, soft-shelled, misshapen or suddenly reduced eggs should prompt attention, especially if more than one bird is affected,” Dr. Casper said. Can people get bird flu from backyard chickens? It’s not common but understanding how bird flu in backyard chickens spreads can help keep you and your family safe. It’s possible if you have close, unprotected contact with infected birds, sick or dead birds or contaminated surfaces. Your risk may be higher if you handle sick or dead birds, clean contaminated coops or touch your face before washing your hands. Children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems should be extra careful around animal and poultry germs in general. Bird flu is being watched closely because flu viruses can change but it’s highly unlikely to get bird flu from an infected person. Bird flu symptoms in people “Bird flu does not always look like ‘flu’ in people. Eye redness or conjunctivitis can be part of the illness,” Dr. Casper said. You should also watch for more typical flu symptoms like: Fever Cough Sore throat Runny or stuffy nose Fatigue Headache Muscle aches Diarrhea Nausea or vomiting When to call a health care provider Call a provider if you develop symptoms after contact with: Sick or dead birds A flock with suspected or confirmed bird flu Contaminated coop surfaces, droppings or equipment Wild birds or poultry that were acting sick Be sure to share your symptoms and tell the provider: What birds you were around Whether birds were sick or dead When the exposure happened Whether you wore gloves, eye protection or a mask Get emergency care if you have: Trouble breathing Chest pain Confusion Severe weakness Blue lips or face Symptoms that are getting worse quickly How to protect yourself and your family Wash hands with soap and water after touching birds, eggs, coops, bedding or equipment. Use hand sanitizer if soap and water are not available. Supervise children to make sure they clean their hands properly. Keep coop shoes outside your home. Supervise children around backyard birds. Do not let them kiss or snuggle birds. Keep birds and poultry supplies out of kitchens, bathrooms, bedrooms and food storage and eating areas. Keep wild birds away from the flock, when possible. Avoid touching your face while caring for birds. Clean equipment properly and keep it outside living areas. Do not eat, drink or smoke while handling birds or cleaning the coop. Wash eggs and handle them safely. What to do if a bird is sick or dead Contact a veterinarian, local agriculture department or health department for instructions. Don’t move birds unless health officials recommend it. Separate sick birds from the flock if you can do so safely and local guidance allows it. Keep children and pets away from the flock. Do not bring sick birds into your home. When to use extra protection Avoid handling sick or dead birds when possible. If you must handle them, use protection including: Disposable gloves Eye protection Well-fitting mask or respirator Boots or boot covers Clothing that can be removed and washed Wash your hands after you remove your protective gear. Wash clothing and clean equipment as directed. If you’re at higher risk for severe illness, avoid handling sick or dead birds when possible. Bottom line Raising backyard chickens and ducks can be rewarding but poultry can also carry germs, including bird flu. Most people are at low risk but flock owners should know the signs of bird flu, avoid touching sick or dead birds with bare hands and practice good backyard poultry safety. If you develop eye redness, stomach symptoms or flu-like symptoms after bird exposure, call your health care provider or a Banner Health expert. Tell them about your bird exposure so they can recommend the next steps for you to take. FAQs about bird flu in backyard flocks Can backyard chickens get bird flu? Yes. Backyard chickens, ducks and other poultry can be exposed to bird flu through wild birds, droppings, contaminated equipment or new birds. Can people get bird flu from backyard chickens? It is uncommon but possible after close contact with infected birds or contaminated surfaces. Basic hygiene and avoiding sick or dead birds can lower your risk. What are signs of bird flu in chickens or ducks? Signs may include sudden death, low energy, poor appetite, breathing problems, swelling, diarrhea, fewer eggs or poor coordination. What symptoms should people watch for after bird exposure? Watch for eye redness, fever, cough, sore throat, fatigue, body aches, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting or trouble breathing. Should children hold or kiss backyard chickens? Children should not kiss or snuggle poultry. They should be supervised around birds and wash their hands afterward. What should I do if one of my birds dies suddenly? Keep children and pets away, do not touch the bird with bare hands and contact a veterinarian or local agriculture or health department. The Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship and the United States Department of Agriculture Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service have found a case of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (H5N1 HPAI) in a multi-species backyard flock in Boone County. This case is Iowa’s seventh detection in 2026. The Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship is strongly encouraging Iowa poultry producers and backyard flock owners to continue bolstering their biosecurity practices and protocols to protect their flocks. The Department has numerous biosecurity resources to reference on its website. Clinical signs of H5N1 HPAI in birds may include: Sudden increase in bird deaths without any clinical signs Lethargy and/or lack of energy and appetite Decrease in egg production Soft, thin-shelled and/or misshapen eggs Swelling of the head, eyelids, comb, wattles, and hocks Purple/blue discoloration of the wattles, comb, and legs Difficulty breathing Coughing, sneezing, and/or nasal discharge (runny nose) Stumbling and/or falling down Diarrhea It remains safe to enjoy eggs and poultry products. As a reminder, consumers should always properly handle and cook eggs and poultry products, including cooking to an internal temperature of 165 ̊F. The Iowa Department of Natural Resources (DNR) asks those who find 5 to 10 or more sick or dead wild birds in a small area to report their findings to local DNR Wildlife Management staff. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) continues to believe the threat to the general public remains low. Any questions related to public health should be directed to the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. If poultry producers or those with backyard birds suspect signs of H5N1 HPAI, they should contact their veterinarian immediately. Possible cases must also be reported to the Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship. This report has been provided by the Iowa Department of Agriculture & Land Stewardship. Support MinneapoliMedia. Support Coon Rapids MN 9-28-2026 6:09am MINNEAPOLIMEDIA NEWS | EARLY BIRD-FLU SURGE HITS MORE THAN 260,000 BIRDS ACROSS MINNESOTA Tom Akaolisa Editor Image ST. PAUL, MN (September 28, 2026). Highly pathogenic avian influenza has returned to Minnesota earlier than animal-health officials expected, with confirmed infections affecting more than 260,000 birds since the beginning of September. Minnesota experienced approximately six weeks without a confirmed outbreak before the virus was identified Sept. 1 in a Wright County commercial flock containing 29,800 birds. Since then, cases have been confirmed in seven commercial flocks and three backyard flocks. The timing is significant because Minnesota officials generally expect the fall outbreak period to begin in October, when migrating waterfowl carry the virus south through the Mississippi Flyway. Officials have not determined why the fall resurgence began several weeks earlier in 2026. Highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly called HPAI or bird flu, can spread rapidly through poultry operations and kill entire flocks within days. When an infection is confirmed, affected birds are generally destroyed, buildings are cleaned and disinfected, and the property must remain empty before poultry can be introduced again. The economic consequences are especially important in Minnesota, which leads the nation in turkey production and raises approximately 45 million turkeys annually. Repeated outbreaks can disrupt individual farms, veterinary-response teams, poultry supplies and international trade. The Minnesota Department of Health reports that no human H5N1 infections have been detected in the state. Health officials continue to monitor people who work with infected animals, while the Board of Animal Health is urging poultry owners to prevent contact between domestic birds and wild waterfowl. Owners who observe unusual illness or bird deaths should contact a veterinarian or Minnesota’s HPAI hotline at 1-833-454-0156. supplementary_news.content: 2026년 10월 2일(금) English 日本語 Latest Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports Entertainment Photos Sports Photos Close the sidebar Studies in Korea link red ginseng to flu responses but urge caution By Kim Myung-ji Published 2026.09.30. 13:37 Prefer Chosunbiz EN on Google A researcher studies how red ginseng affects immunity./Courtesy of As this year's flu season began earlier than usual, studies examining what link red ginseng, known to help with immunity, has with influenza are drawing attention. According to the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency on the 30th, the number of suspected influenza patients per 1,000 outpatients in the first week of September (Aug. 30–Sept. 5) was 25.3, about twice the epidemic threshold of 12.9. With COVID-19 also circulating, the COVID-19 virus detection rate during the same period was 16.3%, and the number of inpatients was 193, more than triple from four weeks earlier. Recent research interest has shifted beyond whether red ginseng simply affects immunity to how it is involved in specific cellular responses and molecular pathways during influenza virus infection. In May last year, a team led by Professor Lee Sang-jun at Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST) treated cells infected with influenza A virus with red ginseng extract and examined the changes. They found differences in the death of infected cells and the expression of viral proteins. In additional experiments, the researchers confirmed that these changes varied depending on the presence of ZBP1, an immune-related protein, and suggested that the ZBP1 pathway may be involved in the process of red ginseng and influenza infection. However, in mouse experiments, the difference in survival rates between the red ginseng group and the control group was not statistically significant. In June the same year, a joint team from KIST, Korea University, and Konkuk University released a study in the international journal Phytomedicine comparing the effects of red ginseng extract—divided into saponin and non-saponin fractions—on influenza A virus. They compared responses to several influenza A virus subtypes (H1N1 and H9N2) not only with the red ginseng extract itself but also with the saponin and non-saponin fractions. In experiments on various lung-derived cells, the researchers observed a pattern of reduced infection levels after treatment with the red ginseng extract and certain fractions for the H9N2 subtype. In contrast, for H1N1, results varied by cell type and treatment method, and in some cells, infection levels and oxidative stress and inflammatory responses even increased. The two studies are assessed as showing that the relationship between red ginseng and influenza can vary depending on the type of virus, the cellular environment, and the components of red ginseng. In an animal study in 2012 involving a team led by Professor Kang Sang-mu at Georgia State University, Korean red ginseng extract showed a protective effect in mice against H1N1 and H3N2 influenza infections. In a domestic study released the same year by Jeonbuk National University College of Medicine and others, a randomized, double-blind clinical trial of 100 healthy adults found that the incidence of acute respiratory infections was lower in the red ginseng group than in the placebo group. However, the study targeted all acute respiratory infections, so it was not a clinical trial that directly confirmed a flu prevention effect. Red ginseng is recognized by the Ministery of Food and Drug Safety as a health functional food ingredient that may help enhance immunity. However, recent influenza-related research has mainly been basic and preclinical studies on cells and animals. An industry official said, "It is hard to directly overinterpret the recent results to mean that taking red ginseng prevents or treats flu in people," and added, "For flu prevention, it is important to follow basic infection prevention practices such as vaccination, handwashing, and ventilation." ※ This article has been translated by AI. Denise Derrer Spears says it’s not completely unexpected. “The wild bird migration is in full swing,” he says. “It’s a little early for the water foul migration, but we know that it’s out there in the environment in Indiana. It’s probably just going to get worse throughout the fall.” This is the first confirmed case in the state since May. The latest detection was found on a commercial meat duck operation in Jay County. More than 24,000 birds have been depopulated, and an approximately 6.2-mile control area with a more than 12-mile surveillance zone in portions of Jay, Adams, and Wells counties has been established. She tells Brownfield the department continues to work with producers to help prevent the spread of HPAI. “We are working with our farmers very closely through all of the quarentine and the depopulation that has to happen,” she says. “We have to make sure that the producers that are located within the surveillance zone are notified as well.” Indiana is a leading producer of poultry, eggs, and poultry products. It ranks first in duck production, third in eggs, third in commercial turkey production, and produces a significant number of broilers. Review Article Open Access 摘要专业翻译 新发病毒性人畜共患病——由病毒从动物储存宿主跨越物种屏障进入人类群体所引发的感染——构成了新发传染病(EID)事件的主体,并已成为全球卫生安全面临的决定性威胁。过去十年间,此类跨物种传播事件的频率持续上升,其驱动因素包括土地利用变化、农业集约化、野生动物贸易及气候变化;与此同时,反向人畜共患病——即人类病原体向动物群体传播——催生了能够孕育未来疫情暴发的新型动物储存宿主。在此背景下,研究人员对2016年1月至2026年6月期间新发病毒性人畜共患病的流行病学证据进行了系统回顾与Meta分析,检索了五个文献数据库并综合了312项纳入研究。年度高后果跨物种传播事件的发生频率以4.98%(95% CI 3.22%–6.76%)的速度递增,该十年间共出现五次《国际卫生条例》下的国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(PHEIC)声明,此外还包括其他高后果跨物种传播事件,如2026年Bundibugyo病毒疫情(病死率[CFR]为30.9%)以及H5N1高致病性禽流感向奶牛群体的扩张。蝙蝠来源病毒呈现最高的合并病死率(29.86%),而灵长类来源病毒则表现出更强的传播能力,支持了毒力–传播力权衡假说。土地利用变化被确认为主导性人为驱动因素,使人畜共患病宿主多样性增加18%–72%。白尾鹿中SARS-CoV-2血清阳性率达到32.7%(95% CI 21.4%–46.1%),并已确认存在鹿向人的回溢传播。非药物干预(NPIs)合计可将有效再生数降低最高达82%,而以预防为导向的One Health策略投资回报率超过1100%。病毒性人畜共患病在人为压力下正加速演进,整合One Health监测体系的上游预防策略是最具成本效益的大流行防范路径。 论文主体内容专业总结 瑞孚迪自动化解决方案>>领 取 1. 引言 论文引言部分系统阐述了新发传染病(EIDs)中人畜共患病的主导地位。研究指出,在1940至2004年间记录的335起EID事件中,60.3%为人畜共患病,其中71.8%源自野生动物。RNA病毒因其高突变率、短世代周期和广泛宿主范围而在新发人畜共患病中占比过高。2016–2026年被视为新发病毒性人畜共患病的分水岭时期:该十年间出现了八次国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(PHEIC)声明中的五次,包括寨卡病毒(2016)、埃博拉病毒(2019,刚果民主共和国)、COVID-19(2020)以及猴痘(2022和2024)。COVID-19大流行本身造成超过7.69亿例确诊感染和690万例死亡。同期,H5N1高致病性禽流感(分支2.3.4.4b)向包括奶牛在内的哺乳动物宿主扩张,引发了对病毒接近持续哺乳动物间传播的担忧。此外,狂犬病每年仍导致约5.9万人死亡,裂谷热通过气候相关的媒介生态变化和牲畜贸易扩展了地理范围,尼帕病毒因其蝙蝠储存宿主、高病死率(55%–70%)及食源性和人际传播能力而维持着高的大流行潜力。引言明确了三项知识空白:缺乏涵盖跨物种传播趋势、传播动力学、人为驱动因素、反向人畜共患病和干预有效性的全面定量综合;反向人畜共患病作为新威胁的证据积累;以及非药物干预(NPIs)效果证据的争议性。 2. 材料与方法 研究严格遵循PRISMA 2020声明,研究方案在数据提取前已在PROSPERO前瞻性注册(注册号CRD420261417296)。检索策略覆盖PubMed/MEDLINE、Web of Science核心合集、Scopus、Embase和CINAHL五个数据库,时间范围为2016年1月1日至2026年6月30日,检索词组合涵盖新发病毒性疾病、流行病学结局(发病率、患病率、病死率[CFR]、续发率[SAR]、基本再生数R0)、驱动因素(土地利用、气候、野生动物贸易)、反向人畜共患病及干预措施(NPI、疫苗接种、监测)五大概念模块。灰色文献通过WHO、FAO、CDC MMWR、ProMED-mail及预印本服务器(medRxiv和bioRxiv)检索,未设语言限制。纳入标准包括报告新发或再发病毒性人畜共患病流行病学、病毒学或生态学数据的原创研究。非随机研究采用MINORS工具评估,病例对照和队列研究采用纽卡斯尔–渥太华量表(NOS)评估,质量评分低于50%的研究被排除出Meta分析但保留于叙述性综合。统计分析采用DerSimonian–Laird随机效应模型,异质性通过I2统计量量化,发表偏倚通过Egger检验和剪补法评估,亚组分析按病原体类型、WHO区域、研究设计和质量评分预设。 3. 结果 3.1. 文献检索与研究筛选 初始检索获得23,120条记录,去除7568条重复后,15,552条记录进入标题和摘要筛选,2987篇进入全文审查,最终312项研究满足全部纳入标准,其中257项提供适合Meta分析的定量数据。纳入研究覆盖全部六个WHO区域的68个国家,研究设计包括84项队列研究、67项横断面研究、52项生态学/建模研究、43项病例对照研究、38项系统回顾/Meta分析和28项干预研究。冠状病毒科(n=127,40.7%)占主导地位,其次为丝状病毒科(n=45,14.4%)和正黏病毒科(n=38,12.2%)。 3.2. 跨物种传播事件的时间趋势 Meadows等人分析了1940–2021年间3998起高后果人畜共患病跨物种传播事件,估计事件频率年增长4.98%(95% CI 3.22%–6.76%),死亡率年增长8.7%(95% CI 4.06%–13.62%),即使排除COVID-19后趋势仍显著。跨物种传播频率的倍增时间约为14年,意味着若当前轨迹持续,疾病负担可能在2040年前再次翻倍。研究人员对2016–2026年数据的泊松回归拟合得出年增长5.3%(95% CI 2.8%–7.9%),与Meadows等人的估计一致。事件频率增长(4.98%)与死亡率增长(8.7%)之间的差异可能反映了对较小跨物种传播事件检测能力的改善,使死亡率趋势成为真实轨迹的更可靠指标。 3.3. 宿主–病毒风险组合 3.3.1. 按病毒来源分类的病死率 Khan等人报告蝙蝠来源病毒的合并病死率为29.86%(I2=99.0%),其中埃博拉病毒为61.06%,尼帕病毒为55.19%,MERS-CoV为18.49%,SARS-CoV为10.86%。极端的异质性表明“蝙蝠来源”并非生物学上有意义的风险类别,方差主要由病毒种水平差异主导。H5N1在禽流感病毒中维持最高记录病死率48.0%(993例确诊,477例死亡),但该数字可能因住院重症病例的检测偏倚而被高估。相比之下,COVID-19的感染病死率显著较低且呈现强烈年龄结构特征。 3.3.2. 毒力–传播力权衡 Guth等人通过Di=Vi×Ti×Ni模型量化了宿主来源与疾病严重程度的关系,其中Vi为毒力(CFR),Ti为传播力(R0),Ni为易感宿主数量。对87种病毒–宿主组合的分析揭示了基本权衡:蝙蝠来源病毒呈现更高毒力(中位CFR 46.6%)但传播力较低,而灵长类来源病毒毒力较低(中位CFR 3.5%)但传播力显著更高。最危险的人畜共患病风险并非位于极端,而在于中等毒力与高效呼吸道传播的组合——H5N1分支2.3.4.4b正接近这一特征谱。 3.3.3. 挑战蝙蝠例外论 Olival等人估计蝙蝠物种每物种携带约17种未发现的人畜共患病毒,高于啮齿类和灵长类物种的约10种。然而,Mollentze和Streicker证明这种超额可由蝙蝠中更大的病毒多样性解释,而非内在特性;在考虑病毒物种丰富度后,人畜共患病风险在哺乳动物目中大致均匀分布。此外,仅凭病毒基因组序列即可以超过70%的准确率预测人畜共患潜力。实际含义是监测应针对具有人畜共患基因组特征的病毒,而不论储存宿主分类学归属。 3.4. 传播途径与疫情规模 合并数据呈现清晰的传播途径层级:呼吸道传播>媒介传播>直接接触>食源性传播>性传播,关键决定因素为单位时间内的潜在传播接触次数。Luo等人报告SARS-CoV-2家庭续发率(SAR)为10.3%,医疗环境SAR为1.0%,公共交通SAR为0.1%。Koh等人从97项研究估计合并家庭SAR为21.1%(95% CI 17.4%–24.8%)。多项疫情调查证实了超过2米的长距离空气传播,Tang等人得出结论所有呼吸道病毒至少部分通过气溶胶传播。媒介传播方面,基孔肯雅病毒R0因媒介物种而异:埃及伊蚊R0=4.1,白纹伊蚊R0=2.8。猴痘(分支IIb)展示了最显著的途径依赖性疫情规模差异:R0在非性网络中为0.006,在性网络中高达7.84,差异超过1000倍。 3.5. 人为驱动因素 3.5.1. 土地利用变化 土地利用变化被确认为主导性人为驱动因素。Gibb等人证明人类土地利用使人畜共患病宿主多样性增加18%–72%,丰度增加21%–144%。Faust等人识别出非线性关系,即中等程度栖息地丧失产生最高跨物种传播风险。Carlson等人预测到2070年气候驱动的分布范围迁移将迫使至少15,000次新型跨物种病毒共享事件。Rohr等人将50%的人畜共患病归因于农业驱动因素。 3.5.2. 野生动物贸易 Gippet等人表明被贸易的哺乳动物物种与人类共享的病原体比非贸易物种多50%。这种放大通过三种机制发生:自然状态下不共存的物种间接触增加;贸易动物的应激诱导免疫抑制和病毒脱落增强;贸易商、市场工人和消费者的职业性暴露。早期COVID-19病例在华南海鲜市场周围的集中进一步印证了野生动物贸易对大流行出现的重要性。 3.5.3. 气候变化 Mora等人报告58%的已知人类致病性疾病可因气候变化而加重,气候驱动的分布范围迁移预计将在行星尺度上重构宿主–病原体互作网络。 3.5.4. 因果链框架综合 Plowright等人的感染–脱落–溢出–传播框架为整合这些驱动因素提供了结构:土地利用变化主要影响“溢出”阶段,气候变化影响“脱落”阶段,贸易/旅行影响“传播”阶段。跨研究的相对排序为土地利用变化>气候变化>野生动物贸易>旅行/流动性。 3.6. 反向人畜共患病与新储存宿主形成 3.6.1. 白尾鹿中的SARS-CoV-2 对九项研究的Meta分析得出白尾鹿SARS-CoV-2合并血清阳性率为32.7%(95% CI 21.4%–46.1%,I2=91.3%)。Kuchipudi等人报告爱荷华州鹿的最高单研究阳性率82.5%。Chandler等人识别出109起独立的人向鹿跨物种传播事件、39起鹿间传播事件和3起鹿向人回溢事件。Pickering等人确认了安大略省鹿中高度分化谱系(B.1.641)与鹿向人传播的系统发育学证据。McBride等人证明SARS-CoV-2在鹿中的进化速度约为人类的3倍。Marques等人发现Alpha变异株在宾夕法尼亚州鹿中持续存在至2023年3月——在人类循环中消失18个月之后——证明鹿可作为不再在人类中循环的病毒变异株的“时间胶囊”。 3.6.2. 养殖水貂中的SARS-CoV-2 Munnink等人记录了荷兰16个水貂养殖场的SARS-CoV-2感染,68%的养殖场工人和接触者被感染,基因组证据确认了水貂向人的传播。丹麦水貂中的cluster 5变异株(Y453F刺突蛋白突变)促使扑杀了1700万只养殖水貂。 3.6.3. H5N1哺乳动物出现 FAO-WOAH-WHO联合风险评估确认了单次禽向牛H5N1跨物种传播事件,随后约4个月的未被发现的牛间传播。Eisfeld等人证明牛源H5N1可同时结合禽类(α2,3-连接)和人类(α2,6-连接)唾液酸受体,这是高效人传人的关键先决条件。关键哺乳动物适应标记包括PB2 M631L及其他PB2和NP替换。Gu等人报告牛源H5N1人类分离株在雪貂模型中具有传播性和致死性。 3.6.4. 新储存宿主形成风险层级 SARS-CoV-2已在数十个国家的超过60种动物物种中被检测到。风险层级为:养殖水貂>白尾鹿>伴侣动物>其他野生动物。关键区分在于维持独立传播循环的物种(鹿和水貂)与终末感染的物种(大多数伴侣动物)。 3.7. 干预有效性 3.7.1. 非药物干预(NPIs) Brauner等人估计将聚集限制在≤10人可使Rt降低42%(95% CI 29%–54%),关闭学校和大学可降低38%(95% CI 16%–54%),居家令仅在其他已实施措施基础上提供额外13%的降低。Flaxman等人估计NPI组合在11个欧洲国家将Rt降低了82%,但该模型受到方法论批评。Bendavid等人发现更严格的NPI相对于较不严格的NPI无显著额外效果。Herby等人得出结论封锁仅将COVID-19死亡率降低了2.0%–3.2%。Haug等人分析了79个地区的6068项NPI,发现干扰较小的NPI可与封锁同样有效。综合证据支持分级方法:针对性聚集限制和学校关闭作为一线措施,大规模封锁保留用于一线措施不足的流行病学必要情况。 3.7.2. 疫苗接种 COVID-19疫苗接种显示对感染的高初始保护,但有效性随时间下降,尤其针对新变异株。Tsang等人证明在高公共卫生和社会措施(PHSM)严格度下合并疫苗有效性为82%(95% CI 80%–83%),在低严格度下为46%(95% CI 41%–50%),表明“渗漏性”疫苗特征与群体水平传播强度相互作用。猴痘JYNNEOS疫苗两剂有效性为66%–90%。 3.7.3. 监测与早期预警 废水监测比临床监测系统提前约1周检测到新出现的SARS-CoV-2变异株,包括尚未在临床采样中出现的隐蔽谱系。动物健康监测系统仍是早期预警的关键但利用不足的组成部分,WOAH/FAO跨界动物疾病渐进控制联合框架(GF-TADs)和OFFLU流感网络提供了可检测动物–人类界面人畜共患威胁的既定兽医监测平台。 3.7.4. One Health策略与成本效益 FAO估计大流行预防成本为每年103–115亿美元,而管理成本为301亿美元,预防具有3:1的成本优势;每年投资30亿美元于One Health方法可产生370亿美元的节省(投资回报率>1100%)。独立建模证实跨物种传播的一级预防相对于大流行应对具有高度成本效益。 4. 讨论 综合得出三项主要发现。第一,人畜共患病跨物种传播在人为压力下加速,高后果事件年增长4.98%,土地利用变化驱动50%的人畜共患病,但大流行防范投资仍以反应性为主。第二,反向人畜共患病创造了当前监测系统未设计检测的新型进化风险:SARS-CoV-2变异株在鹿中持续存在超过18个月,H5N1在奶牛中未被发现的数月传播,均证明动物适应病毒可独立进化并重新出现在人类群体中。第三,证据支持针对性、相称的干预优于一刀切的全人群措施,有效性层级——聚集限制和学校关闭降低Rt 38%–42%,封锁仅提供约13%的边际收益——支持针对特定传播途径的精准公共卫生方法。 4.1. 局限性 统计异质性显著(I2常超过90%),反映病原体、环境和研究设计的真实生物学和方法学多样性。发表和报告偏倚可能因COVID-19研究量的不成比例而存在。地理代表性不均,高收入国家过度代表,而许多人畜共患病储存宿主集中的热带地区代表不足。若干关键数量——特别是H5N1病死率和One Health经济回报——依赖于检测偏倚的病例确定或具有宽不确定性范围的模型预测。跨病原体比较因异质监测基础设施而存在混杂。 5. 结论 2016–2026十年见证了新发病毒性人畜共患病事件的加速,这在统计上稳健且在操作上具有重要意义。三项战略含义:上游预防相对于下游应对系统性资金不足——One Health预防超过1100%的投资回报率要求资源向栖息地保护和野生动物监测重新分配;反向人畜共患病创造了需要扩展关键储存宿主物种基因组监测的新型进化风险,特别关注养殖水貂、鹿科动物和集约化管理牲畜;针对性、相称的干预在有效性和社会成本方面均优于一刀切的全人群措施。兽医部门必须通过投资兽医诊断网络、野生动物疾病监测项目和牲畜生物安全措施全面整合到大流行防范架构中。WOAH PVS路径应作为建设国家One Health能力的框架加以利用,动物健康监测数据必须通过共享平台(如GLEWS+)与人类健康系统实现互操作。人畜共患病跨物种传播的加速步伐,加上反向人畜共患病和协同人为驱动因素,要求整合生态监测、针对性干预和经济优化的结构化One Health应对。不作为的成本——不仅以失去的生命衡量,还以动物储存宿主创造的不断扩大的病毒进化可能性宇宙衡量——远超预防所需的投资。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! supplementary_news.content_title: Minnesota leads nation in avian flu cases as virus returns to turkey flocks
supplementary_news.content: The highly pathogenic avian influenza has struck a third commercial turkey flock in Minnesota, this time in Stearns County. The county is the state's second highest producer of poultry behind Kandiyohi County. File photo By Noah Fish September 30, 2026 at 5:30 AM Minnesota accounts for more than half of the U.S. flocks and birds hit by highly pathogenic avian influenza in the past 30 days, as the virus returns to the state's turkey barns with fall migration. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service has confirmed the virus in 10 Minnesota flocks, totaling 261,450 birds in that span. Seven were commercial flocks and three were backyard flocks. Nationwide, 19 flocks and 517,840 birds in seven states were affected, according to APHIS. Keep Watching MN State Fair 4-H Building Set for Major Renovation South Dakota was second, with three commercial flocks and 135,300 birds. Wisconsin had one commercial flock of 79,100 birds, and North Dakota had one of 41,600. Iowa, Idaho and Montana reported only backyard cases, together fewer than 400 birds. "We've seen kind of a spike here since our state fair last week in cases of high path avian influenza or bird flu coming back into Minnesota in our commercial turkey flocks, and that's a concern," Minnesota Agriculture Commissioner Thom Petersen told Agweek at the Big Iron Farm Show, held Sept. 15-17 in West Fargo, North Dakota. Petersen said cases are not unusual as bird migration starts, but this season is starting out "kind of a little concerning." Minnesota ranks No. 1 in U.S. turkey production. The virus has hit flocks in Wright, Becker, Otter Tail, Big Stone, Kandiyohi, Stearns and Benton counties this month, according to the Minnesota Board of Animal Health. The board's latest confirmations came Sept. 22: 20,531 commercial meat turkeys in Stearns County, plus two flocks of 140 birds each in Benton and Kandiyohi counties. The largest flock hit this fall was 61,111 commercial meat turkeys in Kandiyohi County, confirmed Sept. 16. A flock of 55,318 meat turkeys in Big Stone County was confirmed Sept. 15. On Sept. 10, the board confirmed 44,352 meat turkeys in Becker County and an 18,000-bird commercial breeder operation in Otter Tail County. More livestock news: New Minnesota grant offers more funds toward wolf attack prevention 15h ago New Richland meat processor loses thousands of pounds of product in flash flood 1d ago Tree-Range poultry network resets goals after slower-than-planned growth 2d ago The first case of the fall was a Wright County flock of 29,736 meat turkeys. It was quarantined Aug. 30 and confirmed Sept. 1. The board lists the H5N1 genotype D1.8 for the Wright, Becker and Otter Tail breeder flocks but has not posted a genotype for the later cases. State agriculture officials work closely with the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources on wild bird cases, Petersen said. When people turn in birds such as crows or geese and those birds turn out to have avian influenza, the state can alert farmers nearby. "We can kind of warn the farmers in that area, like, 'Look out for this,' " Petersen said. The board lists nine active cases in Minnesota. The state has recorded 19 infected premises so far in 2026. There were 31 in both 2025 and 2024, 40 in 2023 and 110 in 2022. That brings Minnesota's total to 231 confirmed cases since the first detections on March 25, 2022. About 11 million birds have been affected, according to the board. Commercial turkey meat flocks account for 141 of those cases, more than any other production type. How the response works When a flock tests positive, the farm is quarantined and the birds are depopulated under a USDA flock plan that includes appraisal and indemnity agreements. The carcasses are usually composted inside the barns, which the board says takes about a month. The board also sets up a control area of around 6 miles around each infected farm. Commercial flocks inside it need negative tests and a permit to move birds, poults, manure or litter. Turkey growers shipping birds to slaughter must first go through an eight-day isolation period of stepped-up biosecurity. A second 10-kilometer surveillance zone surrounds the control area, and commercial flocks there must run surveillance testing. An infected farm can restock after the barns are cleaned and disinfected, environmental samples test negative, the barns sit empty for 28 days, and the producer and animal health officials agree on a restocking plan. Reporting sick birds The board asks flock owners to report unexplained deaths, drops in egg production, quiet or depressed birds, and respiratory or neurologic signs such as twisted necks. Reports can go to the Minnesota Avian Influenza Hotline at 1-833-454-0156 or online at bah.state.mn.us/report-sick-birds. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention considers recent bird flu infections in U.S. wild birds and poultry a low risk to the public. I prioritize stories that amplify the power of people. I report out of northeast Rochester, Minnesota, where I live with my wife, Kara, our daughter, Rooney, and polite cat, Zena. HAT Radio Stations Contact Us About HAT Advertise with HAT HPAI Detected in Commercial Duck Flock in Jay County by Hoosier Ag Today September 29, 2026 Highly pathogenic avian influenza has been detected in a commercial meat duck flock in Jay County, according to the Indiana State Board of Animal Health. The affected flock, identified as Jay 14, includes approximately 24,330 ducks. The flock has been placed under quarantine as state and federal animal health officials respond to the detection. A 10-kilometer control area is now active, covering portions of Jay, Adams and Wells counties. A 20-kilometer surveillance zone is also in place, covering portions of Jay, Adams, Blackford and Wells counties. As part of the response, officials are increasing surveillance and testing of poultry and other susceptible animals in and around the affected area. Surveillance Underway The Indiana State Board of Animal Health says testing of nearby non-commercial poultry flocks will help determine whether the virus has spread beyond the affected premises. BOAH staff will contact flock owners within the surveillance zones to offer testing. Wild bird surveillance is also underway. The USDA Wildlife Services and Indiana Department of Natural Resources are assisting with monitoring wild birds in and near the control areas. HPAI has been detected in a variety of wild bird species across the country, including waterfowl such as ducks, geese and swans, as well as raptors and other common bird species. Dairy Farms Also Being Monitored Indiana Grade A dairy farms located within the control areas will also be tested for HPAI. Under a federal order, lactating dairy cattle must have a negative HPAI test before they can move across state lines. USDA has also expanded surveillance by testing milk at the farm or processor level to help establish the health status of individual herds and states. Ongoing National HPAI Response The H5N1 strain of highly pathogenic avian influenza has remained active in the United States since the current outbreak began in February 2022. HPAI has been identified on more than 2,200 premises across all 50 states during that period. The virus has been detected in wild birds, poultry and a range of mammalian species, including dairy cattle, wildlife and humans. State and federal agencies continue to coordinate surveillance and testing of commercial poultry operations, live bird markets and wild bird populations as part of the nation’s ongoing response. For the latest information on Indiana detections, affected premises and response areas, the Indiana State Board of Animal Health’s HPAI dashboard provides updated information. Agriculture and Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen was in Sorrento, Italy on 25 September, where he met Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Food Sovereignty, Francesco Lollobrigida. While there, also delivered a keynote speech at the General Assembly meeting of the Association of Poultry Processors and Poultry Trade in the EU (AVEC), and participate in a panel discussion on ‘Building the Future of the EU Poultry Sector Through Innovation’. This visit comes as member states agreed on the Commission's proposal to provide €73 million to Italy from the agricultural reserve to help compensate farmers in areas affected by outbreaks of avian flu and African swine fever (ASF). A total of €61 million will be provided for poultry and egg farmers in areas affected by avian flu outbreaks between September 2022 and March 2025, while €12.5 million will be provided for pigmeat farmers in areas affected by ASF outbreaks between 1 November 2024 and 30 April 2025. The support will help compensate farmers for losses resulting from measures taken to control and prevent the spread of these animal diseases. The payments, financed by the EU agricultural reserve, must be made to farmers by the end of May next year.
